mainTopic: Whether the לבונה and oil of the חביתין are doubled when there is no כהן גדול; the new פרק opens with the rule that all מנחות are מצה
overview: The amud opens with the חביתין of the כהן גדול in a case where he died and no replacement was appointed yet. In that case a full tenth of סולת is brought both morning and afternoon. The גמרא asks whether the לבונה is doubled according to רבנן, and whether the oil is doubled according to both opinions. רבא tries to prove from the משנה of "five קמצין" that the לבונה is not doubled, and the proof goes back and forth. רב נחמן בר יצחק then brings a ברייתא with exact amounts. The גמרא shows the ברייתא follows אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and concludes that for רבנן too neither the לבונה nor the oil is doubled. רבי יוחנן rules like אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי. When this seems to clash with his rule to follow a סתם משנה, the גמרא answers that two אמוראים reported his view differently. After the הדרן for פרק התכלת, a new משנה teaches that all מנחות are מצה except the חמץ loaves of the תודה and the שתי הלחם. רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and the חכמים then argue about how to leaven those loaves. The גמרא begins by asking for the source that all מנחות are מצה, and רבי אמי starts his answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: According to the Rabbis, is the frankincense doubled too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, according to רבנן, the לבונה is doubled when the סולת is doubled, or stays at its usual amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבנן, is its לבונה doubled or not? Do we say that since its flour was doubled, its לבונה was also doubled? Or maybe what the פסוק revealed, it revealed, and what it did not reveal, it did not reveal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question it does not know the answer to. When the סולת of the חביתין is doubled, does the לבונה get doubled along with it, according to רבנן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to think about it. One side says the לבונה follows the flour, so if the flour doubled, the לבונה doubles too. The other side says we only change what the פסוק tells us to change: it told us about the flour, it said nothing about the לבונה, so the לבונה stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, the spice offered together with a מנחה
Fine flour, the main ingredient of a מנחה
Was doubled
Since / because (one thing follows from the other)
What [the verse] revealed, it revealed; we only learn what is stated and nothing more

steps.confusionAlert: This question is only according to רבנן. Normally רבנן hold that one handful of לבונה is split between morning and afternoon. The question is whether that changes now that the flour is doubled.

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, is its frankincense doubled, or not?
phrases.notes: "Its" means the חביתין offering, in the case where the כהן גדול died and no replacement was appointed yet.

phrases.english: Do we say: since its fine flour was doubled
its frankincense was doubled too,
or perhaps what [the verse] revealed, it revealed,
and what it did not reveal, it did not reveal.
phrases.notes: The פסוק told us the flour is doubled, but it never said anything about the frankincense.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהוּכְפְּלָה סׇלְתּוֹ הוּכְפְּלָה לְבוֹנָתוֹ אוֹ דִילְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question building on the earlier ruling that the סולת is doubled when there is no כהן גדול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, according to רבנן, the amount of לבונה doubles along with the doubled סולת.

steps.title: What about the oil, according to everyone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second question: is the oil doubled too? This question applies both to אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and to רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the oil, both according to אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and according to רבנן, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second, related question. Is the amount of oil also doubled? This is asked according to both opinions, אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לבונה question was only asked according to רבנן, because the two opinions disagree about how the לבונה works. The oil question applies to both opinions, since neither one tells us whether the oil doubles along with the flour.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil mixed into the מנחה
Both ... and ... (according to either opinion)
What is [the law]? A standard way of asking an open question

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁמֶן, בֵּין לְאַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי
phrases.english: And the oil, both according to Abba Yosei ben Dostai
and according to the Rabbis, what is [the law]?
phrases.notes: He means: is the oil also doubled, or does it stay the usual amount?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁמֶן בֵּין לְאַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי וּבֵין לְרַבָּנַן מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel question about a second ingredient, the oil.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the oil of the חביתין doubles along with the סולת, according to both opinions.

steps.title: רבא's proof from the count of five handfuls
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves the לבונה is not doubled. The משנה says there are only five קמצין, but if the לבונה were doubled we would sometimes find seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear: "There are five handfuls." And if it were so, sometimes you would find seven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a משנה to answer the first question, about the לבונה. The משנה lists exactly five cases of a full קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a full handful of לבונה were brought in the morning and another in the afternoon when there is no כהן גדול, those would be two more full handfuls. The משנה would then sometimes have seven, not five. Since the משנה says five, רבא concludes the לבונה is not doubled.

keyTerms.meaning: A handful (plural: handfuls), the measured portion burned on the מזבח
And if it were so; if your idea were correct
Sometimes

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
"There are five handfuls,"
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in מנחות that lists the cases where a full handful is offered.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אִיתָא, זִימְנִין דְּמַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.english: and if it were so, sometimes you would find seven.
phrases.notes: Seven means the usual five plus a full handful of frankincense in the morning and another in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא תָּא שְׁמַע חֲמִשָּׁה קְמָצִין הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the first question (step 1) from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבנן the לבונה is not doubled when there is no כהן גדול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that counts exactly five קמצין; doubled לבונה would sometimes make it seven.

steps.title: The משנה does not count 'what if' cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. The משנה only lists ordinary cases, not unusual "what if" situations like the death of the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not teach cases of "what if."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof. The משנה only counts normal, everyday cases, and a כהן גדול dying is an unusual "what if" case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the משנה being a full and complete list. If the משנה deliberately leaves out unusual situations, then its silence tells us nothing. The next step pushes back on this rejection.

keyTerms.meaning: A case of "if": an unusual, hypothetical situation
He [the תנא] does not teach it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the לבונה is doubled. It only says that רבא's proof does not work. The ברייתא in Step 7 later settles the question.

phrases.english: [Cases of] "if" he does not teach.
phrases.notes: Literally "of 'if' he does not teach." The death of the כהן גדול with no replacement counts as an unusual "if" case.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only; it gives no ruling on the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה's list covers every situation, but the משנה leaves out unusual "what if" cases.

steps.title: But the משנה does count offering a handful outside
steps.stepSummary: While רב פפא was teaching this, רב יוסף בר שמעיה objected. The same משנה lists someone who offers a קומץ outside the Temple, and that is a "what if" case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא was sitting and teaching this הלכה. רב יוסף בר שמעיה said to רב פפא: But [the משנה lists] one who offers up a handful outside, which is a case of "if," and it is taught!
steps.whatsHappening: The first line sets the scene: רב פפא was teaching this discussion. Then רב יוסף בר שמעיה challenges the rejection from step 4. He points out that the משנה does include an unusual case: someone who burns a קומץ outside the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning a קומץ outside the Temple is a sin, not a normal practice, so it is clearly a "what if" case. The משנה still counts it, which shows the משנה does include unusual cases. That cancels the rejection, and רבא's proof works again.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or halachic discussion
Offering up [a sacrifice] outside the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
But look! Opens a challenge that points to a known fact

steps.whatToRemember: רבא proved from the "five קמצין" that the לבונה is not doubled. The rejection said the משנה skips "what if" cases. רב יוסף בר שמעיה showed the משנה does include a "what if" case (offering outside), so רבא's proof holds.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב פָּפָּא וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Pappa was sitting and saying this teaching.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר שְׁמַעְיָה לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Shemaya said to Rav Pappa:
But there is "one who offers up a handful outside,"
which is a case of "if," and it is taught!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר שְׁמַעְיָה לְרַב פָּפָּא וְהָא מַעֲלֶה קוֹמֶץ בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 4 and restores רבא's proof from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the "five קמצין" משנה does not list "what if" cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה lists offering a קומץ outside the Temple, which is clearly an unusual "what if" case. So the משנה does include such cases, and its silence about doubled לבונה is meaningful.

steps.title: So what is the final answer?
steps.stepSummary: After the proof and the challenge went back and forth, the גמרא asks what the final answer is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about this question?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking for the bottom line on the questions from Steps 1 and 2. This line sets up the next move, a new proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף בר שמעיה's objection brought back רבא's proof about the לבונה, but that proof was disputed, and it said nothing about the oil question from Step 2. So the גמרא asks for a clear final answer, and the next step brings a ברייתא that settles both questions.

keyTerms.meaning: What was concluded about it? (asking for the final answer)

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?
phrases.notes: "It" means the questions from earlier: is the לבונה doubled, and is the oil doubled?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth over רבא's proof in Steps 3-5, which dealt only with the לבונה, the גמרא returns to the original questions in Steps 1 and 2 and asks for a decisive resolution.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final ruling on whether the לבונה and the oil are doubled when the סולת is doubled.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a כהן גדול who died
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes a ברייתא. When a כהן גדול dies, a full flour measure is brought morning and afternoon, with two handfuls of לבונה and three לוגין of oil split between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Come and hear a ברייתא. If a כהן גדול died and no replacement was appointed yet, a whole measure of flour is brought in the morning and a whole measure in the afternoon. Two handfuls of לבונה are set aside, one for the morning and one for the afternoon. Three לוגין of oil are set aside, a לוג and a half for the morning and a לוג and a half for the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a ברייתא that lists exactly how much flour, לבונה and oil are used when the כהן גדול has died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the flour is clearly doubled: a whole measure twice a day instead of half twice a day. The ברייתא then tells us the amounts of לבונה (two handfuls) and oil (three לוגין). This should tell us whether those were doubled too.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest
Morning
Afternoon (the later part of the day)
A handful / handfuls, here of לבונה
A unit of liquid measure / units

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
A High Priest who died
and they did not appoint another in his place –
a complete one in the morning,
phrases.notes: "Complete" means a whole עשרון of flour. Normally only half is brought in the morning and half in the afternoon.

phrases.english: and a complete one in the afternoon,
and he separates two handfuls for it –
a handful in the morning and a handful in the afternoon,
and he separates three log for it –
a log and a half in the morning,
a log and a half in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request in Step 6 by bringing a ברייתא that gives exact amounts.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the לבונה and oil are doubled when the flour is doubled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a כהן גדול who died before a replacement was appointed.

steps.title: The ברייתא cannot follow רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ברייתא follows. If it were רבנן, the לבונה would be doubled but the oil would not, and there is no reason for that difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? If you say רבנן, why is the לבונה doubled but the oil not doubled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the ברייתא against רבנן and finds it does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, the normal offering has only one handful of לבונה, so two handfuls would mean the לבונה was doubled. But three לוגין of oil is the normal amount, so the oil was not doubled. Treating the two ingredients differently makes no sense, so the ברייתא cannot be רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is it?
If you say...
What is different? (pointing out an unexplained difference)

phrases.english: Whose is it?
If you say the Rabbis –
what is different about its frankincense, that it was doubled,
and what is different about its oil, that it was not doubled?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִילֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from Step 7 by asking which תנא it follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the ברייתא follows רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבנן the ברייתא would double the לבונה but not the oil, an inconsistency with no reason behind it.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי, who holds that the חביתין always need two handfuls. So in the ברייתא neither the לבונה nor the oil was doubled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי. He said the חביתין of the כהן גדול always need two handfuls. So the לבונה was not doubled, and the oil was not doubled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי. For him, both amounts in the ברייתא are just the normal amounts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי, two handfuls of לבונה is the everyday amount, not a doubled amount. Three לוגין of oil is also the everyday amount. So the ברייתא is consistent: only the flour is doubled, and nothing else.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (switching to a better answer)
The griddle-cake offering of the כהן גדול
In general, normally
Requires

steps.confusionAlert: The two handfuls in the ברייתא are NOT a doubling for אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי. For him, two handfuls is the normal amount every day.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי הִיא,
phrases.english: Rather, it is Abba Yosei ben Dostai,
who said: the griddle-cakes of the High Priest generally
require two handfuls,
so the frankincense was not doubled,
and the oil was not doubled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty of Step 8 by assigning the ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the source to a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא follows רבנן, which would mean the לבונה was doubled and the oil was not.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי, for whom two handfuls is normal, so nothing besides the flour was doubled.

steps.title: Same for רבנן: neither is doubled
steps.stepSummary: Since for אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי the לבונה and oil are not doubled, the same is true for רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since for אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי the oil is not doubled, for רבנן too its לבונה and its oil are not doubled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the final conclusion: for רבנן too, the לבונה and the oil are not doubled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that for אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי, doubling the flour does not double the other ingredients. The גמרא applies the same rule to רבנן. So for them the לבונה stays at one handful and the oil stays at three לוגין. This answers both questions from Steps 1 and 2.

keyTerms.meaning: And since... (drawing a conclusion from a fact)
Also, too
Oil

steps.whatToRemember: When the כהן גדול dies and the flour of the חביתין is doubled, the לבונה and the oil are NOT doubled. This is true for both אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers both questions from Steps 1 and 2: only the flour changes, and the לבונה and oil stay at their usual amounts.

phrases.english: And since the oil, according to Abba Yosei ben Dostai,
is not doubled, its frankincense and its oil,
phrases.notes: The words 'its frankincense and its oil' go with the next line. For רבנן, both of these are not doubled.

phrases.english: according to the Rabbis, are also not doubled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּשֶׁמֶן לְאַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the result of Step 9 for אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and applies it to רבנן, answering the original questions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For both אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and רבנן, when the flour is doubled, the לבונה and the oil are not doubled.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the halacha follows אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה is like אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the back-and-forth, רבי יוחנן gives a final ruling in the dispute: the halacha follows אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי holds that the חביתין always need two handfuls of לבונה, one in the morning and one in the afternoon. רבי יוחנן now says to follow this view in practice. This ruling is what the גמרא will challenge next.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha follows (this opinion)
The daily flour offering of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha is like Abba Yosei ben Dostai.
phrases.notes: He holds the חביתין always need two handfuls of לבונה, as we saw in Step 9.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּאַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the dispute whose views were just clarified in Steps 9 and 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי: the חביתין need two handfuls of לבונה.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוחנן's rule about a סתם משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן could say this, since he also rules like an unnamed משנה, and the unnamed משנה of 'five handfuls' doesn't fit אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say that? But רבי יוחנן said the halacha follows an unnamed משנה, and we learned in a משנה: 'There are five handfuls.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling by pointing to another rule of his: the halacha always follows a משנה that names no author.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unnamed משנה lists only five cases of a handful, and it does not include the חביתין's double handful of לבונה. So that unnamed משנה seems to go against אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי. That means רבי יוחנן's two rules seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: An unnamed משנה, one that states a law without naming who said it
Handfuls (of flour or לבונה taken from a מנחה)
'Did he really say this?' An opening that challenges a statement

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The halacha follows an unnamed Mishnah,
and we learned: There are five handfuls.
phrases.notes: This משנה lists the handful laws and doesn't count a double handful for the חביתין, so it seems to disagree with אבא יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כִּסְתַם מִשְׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling given in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the halacha follows אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן also rules like an unnamed משנה, and the unnamed משנה of 'five handfuls' does not match אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי, so his two rulings contradict.

steps.title: Two אמוראים report רבי יוחנן differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that two different אמוראים disagree about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are different אמוראים, and they argue about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by saying the two statements come from two different students, each reporting רבי יוחנן's view in his own way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One אמורא says רבי יוחנן rules like אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי. The other says רבי יוחנן always rules like an unnamed משנה. There is no contradiction inside one person's view, because these are two separate reports.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They are (different) אמוראים': two scholars who disagree
According to the view of...

steps.whatToRemember: When two statements of one sage seem to clash, the גמרא may answer that different students reported his view differently.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן did not change his mind. The answer is that two later scholars disagree about what he actually held.

phrases.english: They are different Amoraim,
and they argue about the view of Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמוֹרָאֵי נִינְהוּ, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two statements between two different reporters of רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings come from one consistent view of רבי יוחנן, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two אמוראים disagree about רבי יוחנן's view; each statement belongs to a different report.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק התכלת
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of פרק התכלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק התכלת.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק called התכלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional closing line said when finishing a פרק. It is not part of the argument; it just closes the section before a new משנה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the closing line of a פרק
The name of the פרק that is ending, פרק התכלת

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaTecheiles.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ הַתְּכֵלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final ruling and answer.

steps.title: All מנחות are מצה except two
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that all מנחות are brought as מצה, except the חמץ loaves of the תודה and the שתי הלחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All the מנחות come as מצה, except the חמץ loaves of the תודה and the שתי הלחם, which come as חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה that gives a general rule about מנחות and two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that every מנחה must be unleavened. Two offerings are exceptions: the leavened loaves that come with a תודה, and the שתי הלחם. These two are still מנחות; they just have a unique rule that they are baked as חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offerings (flour offerings)
Unleavened bread
Leavened bread
The thanks offering, which comes with loaves of bread
The two loaves offered on שבועות

steps.whyThisMatters: This general rule and its two exceptions set up the whole new פרק, which will discuss how the חמץ loaves are made.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: All the meal offerings come as matza,
except for the leavened loaves of the thanks offering
and the two loaves,
which come as leavened bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַמְּנָחוֹת בָּאוֹת מַצָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All מנחות are brought as מצה, except the חמץ loaves of the תודה and the שתי הלחם, which are brought as חמץ.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: The Leaven Comes From the Dough Itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rules that to make the חמץ loaves, you take leaven out of the measured flour itself and use it to leaven the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: You take the leaven for them from inside the measured dough itself, and use it to make them חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה just said some מנחות are brought as חמץ. Now רבי מאיר explains how to make them rise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot add outside flour to the offering, because the amount of flour is fixed. So רבי מאיר says to set aside part of that same measured flour, let it sour into leaven, and mix it back in.

keyTerms.meaning: Sourdough leaven, a piece of soured dough used to make other dough rise
Separates, takes out
Makes them חמץ (leavens them)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
The leaven, he separates it for them from within them,
phrases.notes: He takes some of the offering's own measured flour and lets it sour into leaven.

phrases.english: and leavens them with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the חמץ loaves mentioned in step 15 are actually leavened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leaven is taken from the offering's own measured flour and used to leaven it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: Put Outside Leaven in the Measure, Then Fill It
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says רבי מאיר's way is not the best. Instead, put leaven into the measuring vessel first, then fill the vessel with flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: That way is also not the best. Instead, you bring leaven, put it into the measuring vessel, and then fill up the vessel with flour.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different method for leavening the loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees the total amount must stay exact. But he uses leaven brought from somewhere else, puts it in the vessel first, and tops it off with flour so the vessel is full.

keyTerms.meaning: The best, most preferred way
The measuring vessel (here, the one for an עִשָּׂרוֹן, a tenth of an איפה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
That too is not the best way,
phrases.notes: He means רבי מאיר's way works, but it is not the ideal way.

phrases.english: rather, he brings the leaven
and puts it into the measuring vessel,
and fills up the measuring vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הִיא אֵינָהּ מִן הַמּוּבְחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר's method and offers a preferred one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The preferred way is to place outside leaven in the measuring vessel and fill the rest with flour.

steps.title: The חכמים Object: The Measure Would Come Out Wrong
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell רבי יהודה that his method would make the offering either less than or more than the required amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: That way too, the offering would end up either short or over the measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבי יהודה's method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point was to keep the flour amount exact. The חכמים say רבי יהודה's method still gets the amount wrong, either too little or too much. The משנה does not say how; the גמרא explains later.

keyTerms.meaning: Lacking, less than the required amount
Extra, more than the required amount

phrases.english: They said to him:
That too would be lacking
or extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַף הִיא הָיְתָה חֲסֵרָה אוֹ יְתֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's method from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's method of putting outside leaven in the vessel and filling it with flour
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The method is supposed to keep the measure exact, but it can leave the offering short of or over the required amount.
steps.whatToRemember: All three opinions agree the flour amount must be exact. They only disagree about how to add leaven without ruining that amount.

steps.title: רבי פרידא Asks: Where Do We Learn All מנחות Are מצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבי פרידא asking רבי אמי for the source that every מנחה must be brought as מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רבי פרידא asked רבי אמי: Where do we learn that all the מנחות must be brought as מצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by asking for the source of the משנה's first rule, that all מנחות are מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the rule but gave no verse. רבי פרידא wants to know which פסוק teaches that every מנחה, not just some, must be מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי פְּרִידָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Perida asked of Rabbi Ami:
From where do we know, regarding all the meal offerings,
that they come as matza?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי פְּרִידָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by asking for the source of the משנה's rule in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches all מנחות must be מצה.

steps.title: רבי אמי Is Surprised: It Is Written Everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי is puzzled by the question. Where the Torah says מצה, it is written. And even where it does not, there is a פסוק that covers it, which he quotes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: "From where do we know?" Where it is written about that מנחה, it is written. And where it is not written about it, it is still written about it:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי begins his answer by questioning why this needs asking. This line sets up the פסוק he is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some מנחות have the word מצה written right next to them, so no question there. For the ones that don't, רבי אמי says there is still a general פסוק covering them. The פסוק itself comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we derive it? (here said with surprise)
It is written about it, the Torah says it explicitly

phrases.english: "From where do we derive it?"
phrases.notes: רבי אמי is surprised by the question itself, as if to say: why would you even ask?

phrases.english: The one about which it is written: it is written about it;
the one about which it is not written: it is still written about it:

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב בַּהּ – כְּתִיב בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering רבי פרידא's question from step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מנחות that say מצה are covered by their own פסוק. The rest are covered by a general פסוק, which is quoted next.
